tina_support: Hey team — triaging ticket #48721. Customer in London reports requests that should hit eu-west-1 are landing in us-east-1 for the last ~4h. They see `x-region: us-east-1` in responses and ~350ms extra latency. They repro'd from home and mobile networks.

rob_oncall: Can you paste the exact response headers + the curl you used? Also which resolver did the customer show?

tina_support: Pasting the curl output they provided:

```
$ curl -s -D - -o /dev/null "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED"
HTTP/2 200 
x-region: us-east-1
x-latency-ms: 420
server: redwood-edge
```

ISP reported: BT, resolver 212.159.6.5. TTL on A record we show is 60.

anya_netops: Hmm. That IP (212.159.6.5) is an ISP resolver likely caching an old mapping or not honoring EDNS/geo. Can you run `dig +short @212.159.6.5 api.redwood.ai` and `dig +trace api.redwood.ai` from your side?

tina_support: Ran quick digs from a proxy to reproduce:
```
$ dig @212.159.6.5 api.redwood.ai A +short
54.174.23.11
$ dig +trace api.redwood.ai
; -> got 54.174.23.11 from resolver
;; Received 60.0 TTL
```
So the resolver is returning our us-east IP (54.174.23.11).

kevin_sre: 54.174.23.11 maps to our US anycast/edge. Two likely causes: 1) ISP cache still has old A record pointing at US IP from last night's rollout, or 2) EDNS-client-subnet / GeoIP DB mapping is resolving that resolver to US. We also did a eu VIP roll last night, that could have left some stale entries.

anya_netops: We rolled the EU VIP ~02:30 UTC and lowered TTL to 300 but some ISPs ignore short TTLs. A subset of resolvers will hold mappings longer. Also some resolvers don't pass EDNS ECS so GeoIP fallback can pick a non-optimal POP.

rob_oncall: Short repro checklist for us —
- confirm customer resolver IP (done)
- check our DNS provider logs for queries from that resolver (WIP)
- confirm BGP announce state for the EU prefix (check with net vendor)
- ask customer to query via 1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8 as a quick test.

tina_support: Customer tested 1.1.1.1 and then requests started hitting eu-west-1 (confirmed by `x-region: eu-west-1`). So this is definitely resolver-side caching. Customer can't change ISP. They asked if we can do anything server-side to avoid cross-region hits (cost + QoS). :thinking:

kevin_sre: Short-term mitigations we can consider:
- ask network partner to request purge/flush for that resolver if vendor supports it (some CDNs will do cache purge by IP)
- temporarily announce the EU prefix from a more specific BGP path to bias routing back to EU (requires infra ops coordination)
- create an eu-specific hostname (eu.api.redwood.ai) and return a 302 to it — but initial TCP handshake still goes to whichever IP resolver gave them, so this won't avoid the first cross-region connection
- lower TTL and roll out again, but many ISPs ignore TTLs as noted.

anya_netops: We're opening an immediate vendor escalation for a cache purge and checking the BGP state now. I've also asked infra to verify we didn't accidentally withdraw the EU announcement during the rollout.

rob_oncall: I pushed a runtime tweak that will add an `X-Region-Preference: eu` header for requests coming from UK IP ranges; runtime will try to prefer eu backend where possible. This is a partial mitigation (works for new connections we control).

tina_support: Customer reported improvement after ~03:50 UTC — most traffic now hits eu but occasional requests still land in us-east. They'll keep an eye for a day.

kevin_sre: Follow-ups:
- NetOps confirm whether EU prefix announcement was briefly withdrawn (report due in 30m).
- Vendor cache purge ticket created (V-1192).
- Create a short internal postmortem if vendor confirms stale cache/TTL non-compliance.

routebot: :rotating_light: Monitor created: M-4892 "geo-mismatch spike" — alerting on % of requests with `x-region` != expected. Added to watchlist.

rob_oncall: Notes for support team: when you see this again, ask customer for `dig @<their-resolver> api.redwood.ai +short` and a `traceroute` to the returned IP. That evidence helps NetOps escalate BGP/cache issues faster.

tina_support: Thanks all — I'll update the customer with the mitigation steps and keep the ticket open until vendor confirms cache purge. :thumbsup:
